meta.audience: The five messengers, the judges, and the multitude
meta.location: The judgment-seat, the prison, the burial, and the house of Seantum
principles: An accusation that fits the accuser
A prediction given as a script

world_behind.title: Five men set their own test
world_behind.text: Verse 2 has them stating what they do not believe and what would change it: if the judge is dead, the rest is true.

world_behind.title: They are arrested for the murder
world_behind.text: Verses 7 through 9 have a crowd that knows nothing of the garden find five men prostrate by the body and conclude that God struck them. Helaman 7:10 puts Nephi's tower in his garden by the highway to the chief market, so the two crowds of these chapters formed a few hundred yards apart and never met.

world_behind.title: The judges learn the five are their own messengers
world_behind.text: Verses 12 and 13 have them asking for the five and being told there are only murderers in prison.

world_behind.title: The accusation against Nephi is conspiracy
world_behind.text: Verse 16 has the judges proposing that he arranged the murder to make himself a prophet.

world_behind.title: They offer money and his life
world_behind.text: Verse 20 offers a bribe and a pardon in one sentence on condition of naming a partner. Helaman 7:5 had charged the judges with letting the guilty go unpunished because of their money; this verse shows the same currency being offered rather than taken.

world_behind.title: Nephi answers with a second sign written as dialogue
world_behind.text: Verses 26 through 36 script the whole interview in advance: the questions to ask Seantum, his replies, the blood on the skirts of his cloak, and his confession, in order. Nothing else in the volume gives a prophecy as a transcript of a conversation that has not happened yet.

world_behind.title: The people divide three ways
world_behind.text: Verses 39 through 41 split the crowd four ways, ending with some who call him a god. Alma 18:2 to 5 has king Lamoni's servants reach the same conclusion about Ammon, and Alma 19:25 has the crowd argue it out. The record reports this misreading twice and corrects it both times.

words.text: Clothing, and by extension a disguise. The word occurs once in all of scripture, here, in the phrase "a garb of secrecy" describing how the brother got close enough to stab.
To expose or catch out. This is its one appearance in all of scripture, here, where the judges announce their plan to make Nephi confess and name the real killer.
Allied by agreement. Treated at 2 Nephi 17:2, in quoted Isaiah, of Syria allied with Ephraim. The judges use it as a criminal charge.
Knew. The record uses the word twice, here and at 3 Nephi 11:8, and the King James Bible thirteen times. Nephi predicts that Seantum will not know what to say.
The lower edges of a garment. It appears once in the record, and seven times in the King James Bible, including Jeremiah 2:34, where blood is found in the skirts of a nation.
Loss of color from the face. The word occurs once in the record and once in the King James Bible, at Jeremiah 30:6. Nephi names it in advance as the evidence the questioners should point to.

phrases.term: We will know of a surety whether this man be a prophet
phrases.text: Five unbelievers designing their own experiment. They state the disconfirming condition before they run to check it.

phrases.term: The chief judge had fallen to the earth, and did lie in his blood
phrases.text: The sentence Helaman 8:27 had already written. Mormon repeats the wording so the reader sees the prediction land.

phrases.term: He being stabbed by his brother by a garb of secrecy
phrases.text: The murder reported in the middle of the aftermath. The killer got close by looking like someone who belonged there.

phrases.term: These men are they who have murdered the judge, and God has smitten them
phrases.text: A crowd reasoning correctly from what it can see and arriving at the wrong answer. Verse 8 notes that they knew nothing of the garden.

phrases.term: Concerning this five whom ye say ye have sent, we know not
phrases.text: The moment the story doubles back. The judges' own messengers are the prisoners, and nobody in either group knows it.

phrases.term: We know that this Nephi must have agreed with some one to slay the judge
phrases.text: The theory the judges propose. Men who belong to a murderous band explain a murder by imagining a conspiracy.

phrases.term: Behold here is money; and also we will grant unto thee thy life
phrases.text: Payment and pardon offered together for a name. Alma 11:22 had Zeezrom making the same kind of offer to Amulek.

phrases.term: O ye fools, ye uncircumcised of heart, ye blind, and ye stiffnecked people
phrases.text: Nephi's answer to the bribe. He takes neither the money nor the terms of the question.

phrases.term: Ye shall find blood upon the skirts of his cloak
phrases.text: The detail that turns the interview. It is physical, checkable, and given before anyone has looked.

phrases.term: Then shall ye know that I am an honest man, and that I am sent unto you from God
phrases.text: The purpose of the whole script. The sign is designed to settle the accusation of verse 16 rather than to impress.

phrases.term: He is a god, for except he was a god he could not know of all things
phrases.text: The conclusion some of the people draw. Alma 18:2 had Lamoni reaching for the same category about Ammon.

verses.label: v. 2
verses.title: The sceptics design the test, and it is a fair one
verses.text: The record puts the experiment in the mouths of the people who doubt: "now we will know of a surety whether this man be a prophet and God hath commanded him to prophesy such marvelous things unto us." What they propose is to run to the judgment-seat and look. The claim being tested is specific, checkable within minutes, and the check is not the prophet's idea. A record wanting an easy vindication would not have the opposition set the terms.

verses.label: v. 4–5
verses.title: Belief reported in two stages, with the interval named
verses.text: The record separates the shock from the conclusion: "when they saw this they were astonished exceedingly, insomuch that they fell to the earth; for they had not believed the words which Nephi had spoken concerning the chief judge." Verse 5 gives the change and its consequence: "when they saw they believed, and fear came upon them lest all the judgments which Nephi had spoken should come upon the people." What frightens them is not the corpse but the rest of the prophecy, which the corpse has just made credible.

verses.label: v. 14–15
verses.title: Witnesses who mark the edge of what they know
verses.text: The record has the five give their account and then stop precisely: "as for the murder of this man, we know not who has done it; and only this much we know, we ran and came according as ye desired, and behold he was dead, according to the words of Nephi." The phrase only this much we know separates what they saw from what they cannot say. The record keeps the disclaimer, which is what makes the testimony worth anything.

verses.label: v. 16–17
verses.title: A counter-theory built from the prophet's own accuracy
verses.text: The record has the judges turn the successful prediction into evidence of a plot: "we know that this Nephi must have agreed with some one to slay the judge, and then he might declare it unto us, that he might convert us unto his faith." Verse 17 states the plan that follows from it, "we will detect this man, and he shall confess his fault and make known unto us the true murderer." Foreknowledge is read as complicity, which is the only alternative to prophecy the argument allows.

verses.label: v. 37–41
verses.title: One confirmed prediction, four different conclusions
verses.text: The record reports the test passing, "they went and did, even according as Nephi had said unto them. And behold, the words which he had said were true," and then declines to report a single response. Some believed on his words; some "believed because of the testimony of the five"; some "said that Nephi was a prophet"; and others "said: Behold, he is a god, for except he was a god he could not know of all things." A verified prophecy produces a split audience, and the record lists the positions instead of resolving them.

chapter.title: Unbelievers set the terms and keep them
chapter.text: Verse 2 has the five naming their own test, and verses 4 and 5 have them believing when it comes out. The record lets skeptics run the experiment.

chapter.title: A reasonable inference is wrong
chapter.text: The crowd in verse 8 sees five men prostrate beside a corpse. Mormon supplies the missing fact in the same verse: they knew nothing of the garden.

chapter.title: The accusation describes the accusers
chapter.text: Verse 1 counts the men who ran, "there were five who went," and verse 2 quotes their reasoning before they arrive, "we do not believe that he is a prophet." Helaman 8:1 and 8:4 have already identified some of the judges present as belonging to Gadianton's band, and Helaman 9:38 records the murderer confessing. The charge those judges bring against Nephi at verse 16 is that he agreed with a confederate; the record has already told the reader which party in the room actually works that way.

chapter.title: Bribery and pardon are one offer
chapter.text: Verse 20 puts money and a life on the table for a name. The judicial process of Helaman 7:5 is shown working from the inside.

chapter.title: The second sign is written as a transcript
chapter.text: Verses 27 through 36 give both sides of a conversation that has not happened. Verse 37 reports it went that way.

chapter.title: The evidence is physical and checkable
chapter.text: Verses 26 through 36 give a script of eleven steps, each stating in advance what the suspect will do. Three of them are physical and checkable on the spot: "ye shall find blood upon the skirts of his cloak" at verse 31, "then shall he tremble, and shall look pale" at verse 33, and the confession at verse 35. Verse 37 reports the test run and confirms it in the record's own words, "the words which he had said were true; for according to the words he did deny; and also according to the words he did confess." Nothing in the procedure requires taking the prophet's word for anything unseen.

chapter.title: The five become witnesses
chapter.text: Verse 39 says some believed because of their testimony, converted while in prison for a murder they did not commit.

chapter.title: The people overshoot
chapter.text: Verse 41 has some concluding he is a god. The chapter that clears him of one wrong idea ends with another forming.

applications.title: State what would change your mind, then go look
applications.text: The five named their condition before they ran. Deciding in advance what evidence would count keeps a test honest.

applications.title: Hold the obvious reading loosely
applications.text: A crowd found five men by a body and got it exactly wrong. Ask what you would be missing if the obvious reading were false.

applications.title: Report only what you actually know
applications.text: The five said plainly that they did not know who had done the murder, and then stated the small thing they did know. Under suspicion the pull is to supply a theory, and the credible witness marks the edge of his knowledge instead.

applications.title: Notice when an accusation matches the accuser
applications.text: People often explain events with the mechanism they know best. What someone imagines you did can describe them.

applications.title: Watch what gets offered alongside the accusation
applications.text: The judges demanded a confession and in the same breath offered Nephi money and his life. Pressure that arrives bundled with a payment tells you the people applying it are not confident of the case.

applications.title: Make the check something anyone can run
applications.text: Nephi pointed at blood on a cloak. When you want to be believed, offer the thing that can be examined rather than the thing that must be trusted.

applications.title: Something can still happen in the worst room
applications.text: The five were converted while they sat in prison on a charge they had not earned. A stretch you would never have chosen is still a stretch in which something can change.

applications.title: Correct the flattery as quickly as the slander
applications.text: Some concluded that Nephi must be a god, since nobody else could have known. Being overestimated is a misreading too, and it is harder to refuse because it arrives as praise.

questions.text: What would actually change my mind, and have I said it out loud?
What have I concluded from partial information lately?
What do I accuse others of that I would recognize in myself?
What has been offered to me for saying what someone wanted?
Where am I uncircumcised of heart?
What would it take for people to know I am honest?
What have I over-credited because I could not explain it?
